history.period: CONFLICT (verify): the lingam is described as Panchmukhi (five-faced) in most popular sources and the ASI-era descriptions, but the Wikipedia/architectural literature calls it Chaturmukh (four-faced)
history.summary: CLOSELY RELATED SUB-ENTRY of seq 1348 (Mundeshwari Devi Temple) - NOT a separate temple; it is the famous five-faced Shivalinga enshrined at the centre of the sanctum of the Mundeshwari temple complex at Ramgarh, Kaimur. Popular belief (local tradition, UNVERIFIED) holds that the lingam's colour changes with the sun's position, and that it changes colour every three days; the shrine also draws attention for the temple's unique bloodless goat-sacrifice ritual. A large Nandi statue stands on the west side of the main entrance. Written as its own file because the CSV lists it as a separate row, but the shrine's history is the history of the Mundeshwari complex (see seq 1348); it shares the same festivals, hours, travel and dating conflicts.

name: Panchmukhi Shivalinga Shrine, Mundeshwari Complex
town_description: Ramgarh is a village at the foot of the Mundeshwari Hills on the Kaimur plateau in Kaimur (Bhabua) district, southwestern Bihar, near the Son river. It is the base for the ancient Mundeshwari hilltop shrine, now developed with roads, stairs, resting areas and an eco-park. The nearest towns are Bhabua (district HQ) and Mohania, with rail and road links toward Varanasi and Patna.

travel.airport: Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport, Varanasi, ~102 km
travel.railway: Mohania - Bhabua Road railway station, ~22 km by road
travel.road: Reachable by road via Patna, Gaya or Varanasi; the hilltop is now served by roads and stairs with public amenities

visitor_information.best_time: October-March for weather; Ramnavami, Shivratri and Navaratra for the mela (very crowded)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Same as the Mundeshwari complex: opens half an hour before sunrise, closes at sunset; noon-12:20 pm break (verify). Entry free.
